St. Sophronius of Jerusalem

Saints

Saint Sophronius of Jerusalem

St. Sophronius of Jerusalem · St. Sophronios of Jerusalem · St. Sophronius the Wise

Period
c.560–638; patriarch 634–638 (OCA Church History chronology)
Region
Damascus; Palestine; Alexandria; Jerusalem
Titles / vocation
Hierarch · Teacher
Commemoration
March 11

Introduction

Saint Sophronius was a monk, writer, and Patriarch of Jerusalem who opposed teachings that diminished Christ’s human activity or human will.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Repose in 638 in the OCA Church History chronology; not described as martyrdom

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Born in Damascus around 560, he received a classical education before seeking monastic life. With John Moschus he visited monasteries and collected accounts of ascetics. Those encounters stand behind the Spiritual Meadow tradition.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Opening paragraphs on Damascus, monastic journeys and John Moschus

Life and notable events

Wars displaced him through Palestine, Egypt, and Rome. He eventually became Patriarch of Jerusalem. His final ministry coincided with the siege and surrender of Jerusalem, placing the local Christian community under new political rule.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on travel, patriarchate and the siege of Jerusalem

In 633 he opposed monoenergism, the teaching that Christ has only one divine-human activity. As patriarch he also opposed monothelitism, which asserts only one will in Christ. His resistance helped prepare the later defense of Christ’s fully divine and fully human willing.

[2] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on Sophronius’s appeal to Cyrus and his Jerusalem patriarchate

Death and martyrdom

The Saint’s life describes his grief during Jerusalem’s ordeal and records his death without a martyr’s execution. The OCA’s Church History gives 638; its separate Saint’s life prints a different terminal date for his patriarchate.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Closing account of the siege and death; compare Church History chronology

Writings and legacy

The ecclesiastical source associates him with dogmatic writing, hymnography, monastic texts, and the received Life of Saint Mary of Egypt. These traditional attributions should remain distinguished from a modern critical catalogue.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Closing paragraphs on dogmatic and liturgical writings
